asm:activation.text: Replace the floor by a switch, % \begin{keyresult}{A}{eq:solvable-activation} \Gam(a,\fconv,\Mmem)=\Gamz\,\actS(a)\,e^{\alpha \fconv+\beta \Mmem}, \qquad \actS(a)=\frac{a^{p}}{a^{p}+\aact^{p}} , \end{keyresult} % with the exponent $p$ constrained by \cref{prop:activation} below.
asm:activation.title: Activation

asm:closure.text: Space is flat and FLRW. The precursor $\rhoI$ and the localized product $\rhoD$ are pressureless, the third product is an exact vacuum with $p_V=-\rhoV$, and baryons and radiation are separately conserved. A fraction $\bfrac\in[0,1]$ of the converted energy feeds the localized product and the rest feeds the vacuum. No other sector of negative pressure is present.
asm:closure.title: Homogeneous closure

asm:geodesic.text: The theory is \emph{defined} by imposing \cref{eq:perturbations-integrability} with a geodesic clock, so that the volumetric transfer is spatially uniform on comoving hypersurfaces, \cref{eq:perturbations-com}. Equivalently, the local conversion rate anti-correlates exactly with the local precursor density, $\delta\Gam/\bar\Gam=-\delta_I$. The kinetic variables $(\fconv,\Mmem)$ are then \emph{diag
asm:geodesic.title: Geodesic realization

asm:rate-regularity.text: $\Gam$ is non-negative, bounded above by $G<\infty$, and uniformly Lipschitz in $(\fconv,\Mmem)$ on $[0,1]^2$; the initial conditions converge in probability.

cor:b-invisible.text: Every linear observable built from $\delta_{\rm m}$, $\vartheta$ and the metric potentials depends on the model only through $\Hub(a)$ and $\gamma_c(a)$. In particular $\bfrac$, and the split of the dark sector into precursor and defects, cannot be measured by any linear probe.

cor:memory-invisible.text: The memory parameters $(\beta,\tauM)$ affect \cref{eq:positivity-no-sign-flip} only through the scalar $\Gam\ge0$. They can change the magnitude of $\delta_{\rm eff}$ by a bounded factor and shift the epoch at which it peaks, but they cannot change its sign.
cor:memory-invisible.title: Memory does not enter the sign

cor:one-transition.text: With $\rhom=\rhoI+\rhoD+\rhob$ and $\mathcal A=\ddot a/a$, % \begin{keyresult}{I}{eq:cosmology-monotone-acceleration} \dot{\mathcal A} =\frac{3\QV+3\Hub\rhom+8\Hub\rhor}{6\Mpl^2}\ge0 , \end{keyresult} % strictly when matter or radiation is present. A solution that begins decelerating and satisfies \cref{thm:de-sitter} therefore crosses $\mathcal A=0$ exactly once. A history requiring several late
cor:one-transition.title: At most one transition

def:memory.text: Along a flow line with proper time $\tau$, % \begin{equation}\label{eq:process-memory} \tauM\,\odv{\Mmem}{\tau}=\fconv-\Mmem,\qquad \tauM>0 , \end{equation} % whose solution from $\tau_i$ is % \begin{equation}\label{eq:process-memory-solution} \Mmem(\tau)=\Mmem_i e^{-(\tau-\tau_i)/\tauM} +\frac{1}{\tauM}\int_{\tau_i}^{\tau}e^{-(\tau-s)/\tauM}\fconv(s)\,\dd s . \end{equation}
def:memory.title: Memory variable

prop:activation.text: Under \cref{asm:activation} with $\bfrac<1$, the limit $V_{\rm early}=\lim_{a\to0^+}\rhoV(a)$ exists and is finite, $\rhoV$ is non-decreasing, and therefore $\rhoV\ge0$ on $(0,1]$ if and only if $V_{\rm early}\ge0$. The vacuum increment is $\rhoV_0-V_{\rm early}=(1-\bfrac)\int_0^1\Gam\rhoI\,\dd a/(a\Hub)$, so with $\rhoI\propto a^{-3}$ and a radiation-dominated deep past the integrand behaves as $
prop:activation.title: Convergence and positivity

prop:bridge.text: If each of $N$ precursor units per patch can nucleate once, and the $(k+1)$-th event has rate $\Gam_k=\Gam(h_0+k\mathsf{q})$, then $K_t$ is exactly the chain of \cref{eq:process-intensity} with $\Gam(\fconv)=\Gam(h_0+\fconv N\mathsf{q})$. The exponential law \cref{eq:process-rate} corresponds to $\log\Gam$ linear in $h$ over the relevant range, with $\alpha=N\mathsf{q}\,\dd\log\Gam/\dd h$. Reinfor
prop:bridge.title: The event sequence is a reinforced birth process

prop:classical-reduction.text: With the jump operators \cref{eq:quantum-collective}, which map each occupation basis state to a single basis state and have diagonal $\jump_i^{\dagger}\jump_i$, populations decouple from coherences. The populations obey exactly the birth chain with rates $(N-k)\Gamz e^{\alpha k/(N-1)}$, and coherences decay at rate at least $\Gam/2$.
prop:classical-reduction.title: Exact classical reduction

prop:clock.title: Clock field equations

prop:clumping-unstable.text: If instead $\delta \rhoV_{\rm com}=\zeta\,\delta_I$ with $\zeta>0$, the dust experiences a force $\rhoI A^i=\partial^i \rhoV$, and the growth equation acquires a term $-k^2\zeta\delta/(a^2\bar\rho_I)$. The effective sound speed squared is then negative and short-wavelength modes grow without bound.
prop:clumping-unstable.title: A clumping vacuum is gradient-unstable

prop:derrick.text: In three spatial dimensions let $E[\phi]=E_2+E_0$ with $E_2=\tfrac12\int|\nabla\phi|^2$ and $E_0=\int W(\phi)$, both finite and $W\ge0$ after subtracting the vacuum. Under $\phi_\sigma(\mathbf x)=\phi(\sigma\mathbf x)$ one has $E(\sigma)=\sigma^{-1}E_2+\sigma^{-3}E_0$, so a non-trivial stationary point would require $E_2+3E_0=0$, impossible for $E_2>0$.
prop:derrick.title: Derrick scaling

prop:determined-V.text: Fix $(\Gamz,\alpha,\beta,\tauM,\bfrac)$, the activation law, and initial data. By \cref{thm:regular-future} the background is unique, so with $\clock=t$, % \begin{keyresult}{I}{eq:realizations-determined-V} V(\clock)=V_0+(1-\bfrac)\int_{t_0}^{\clock}\Gam\rhoI\,\dd t , \qquad \lagm=\rhoI+\rhoD , \end{keyresult} % is a five-parameter family, monotone non-decreasing and bounded above by \cref{eq:cosm
prop:determined-V.title: Kinetically determined potential

Let $C_{\mu

prop:four-form.title: Four-form vacuum

prop:ide-map.text: With $\rhodmeff=\rhoI+\rhoD$ and $s=\rhoI/\rhodmeff$, % \begin{keyresult}{I}{eq:positivity-map} \QV=\xieff\,\Hub\,\rhodmeff , \qquad \xieff=\frac{(1-\bfrac)\Gam s}{\Hub}\ \ge 0 . \end{keyresult} % The model reduces to the standard coupling $Q=\xi \Hub\rho_{\rm dm}$ with constant $\xi$ if and only if $\bfrac=0$ and $\Gam=\xi \Hub$. It can never take the form $Q\propto\rho_{\rm de}$.
prop:ide-map.title: Exact map

prop:identities.text: With $a_i=1$, constant $\bfrac$ and $\fconv_i<1$, the system \cref{eq:cosmology-system} satisfies % \begin{keyresult}{I}{eq:cosmology-survival} \rhoI a^3=\rho_{I,i}\,\frac{1-\fconv}{1-\fconv_i}, \qquad \rhoD a^3=\rho_{D,i}+\bfrac\,\rho_{I,i}\,\frac{\fconv-\fconv_i}{1-\fconv_i} , \end{keyresult} % and, wherever $\dot \fconv>0$, % \begin{keyresult}{I}{eq:cosmology-dVdf} \odv{\rhoV}{\fconv}=\frac{(1-
prop:identities.title: Survival and product identities

prop:memory-origin.text: Attach to each unit $i$ an internal variable $m_i\in[0,1]$ relaxing towards that unit's own state $s_i\in\{0,1\}$, $\tauM\dot m_i=s_i-m_i$. Then the population mean $\Mmem=N^{-1}\sum_i m_i$ obeys \cref{eq:process-memory} exactly, for every $N$ and every realisation.
prop:memory-origin.title: Memory as an eliminated degree of freedom

prop:no-instability.text: Under \cref{asm:geodesic} the system \cref{eq:perturbations-system} contains no independent dark-energy degree of freedom, no pressure perturbation, and no $k$-dependent coefficient. Its coefficients are of order $\Hub$ and $\Hub^2$, so $|\delta_{\rm m}|$ is bounded by a power of $a$ on every scale.
prop:no-instability.title: Absence of the instability

prop:no-rolling.text: For a canonical real scalar with $\Lag=-\tfrac12(\covd\phi)^2-W(\phi)$ one has $\rho_\phi+p_\phi=\dot\phi^2$. Hence $w_\phi=-1$ exactly requires $\dot\phi=0$.
prop:no-rolling.title: No rolling exact vacuum

prop:recipient-proportional.text: Consider two sectors with $\dot\rho_1+3\Hub\rho_1=-Q$ and $\dot\rho_2+3\Hub(1+w)\rho_2=+Q$. If $Q=\xi \Hub\rho_2$ with $\xi>0$, then on the face $\{\rho_1=0\}$ the field is $\dot\rho_1=-\xi \Hub\rho_2<0$ whenever $\rho_2>0$: the subtangent condition fails on a set of codimension one, and $\rho_1$ is driven through zero. The same argument with the roles exchanged applies to $Q=\xi \Hub\rho_1$ drain
prop:recipient-proportional.title: Recipient-proportional couplings are not positivity-safe

prop:survival.text: For $\Gam\ge0$ locally integrable along the solution and $\fconv_i\in[0,1)$, % \begin{keyresult}{I}{eq:process-survival} 1-\fconv(t)=(1-\fconv_i)\exp\left[-\int_{t_i}^{t}\Gam(s)\,\dd s\right] , \end{keyresult} % so $\fconv_i\le \fconv(t)<1$ at every finite time, and $\fconv\to1$ if and only if $\int^{\infty}\Gam\,\dd s$ diverges.
prop:survival.title: Survival

prop:unitary-obstruction.text: Let $\Hilb$ be finite-dimensional, $U(t)=e^{-iHt/\hbar}$ unitary, and $\mathcal A\subset\Hilb$ a subspace with $U(t)\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal A$ for all $t\ge0$. Then $U(t)\mathcal A=\mathcal A$ and $U(t)\mathcal A^{\perp}=\mathcal A^{\perp}$, so the probability of occupying $\mathcal A$ cannot increase by transfer from its complement.
prop:unitary-obstruction.title: No absorption under unitary flow

rem:hazard-time-change.text: \Cref{asm:rate-regularity} requires a bounded rate, which fails wherever the rate is driven by a diverging compression. For the converted fraction nothing is lost, though \cref{rem:residual-boundary-layer} shows that the same is not true of the residual density. Let $\Lambda(t)=\int_{t_i}^{t}\Gam\,\dd s$ be the cumulative hazard and change time to $\Lambda$. If $\Gam$ does not depend on the state,
rem:hazard-time-change.title: The boundedness hypothesis can be traded for a time change

rem:hysteresis-prescribed.text: The hypothesis is not cosmetic and cannot be removed by rewording. The comparison argument below compares two solutions of one system, so both must be driven by the same $a(t)$; and the conclusion is that they accumulate different vacuum, which through the Friedmann constraint would give them different $a(t)$. Stated for the coupled system the theorem would therefore contradict its own hypothesis.
rem:hysteresis-prescribed.title: Why the expansion history is prescribed

rem:jerk-neutrinos.text: The last hypothesis is there because the fits of \cref{sec:observations} carry one massive neutrino eigenstate, which is neither pressureless nor conserved radiation, so a bound advertised as parameter-free must say what it does with it. Such a species contributes $-\tfrac32\dot p/(2\Mpl^2\Hub^3)$ to $\jerk$, and its pressure falls monotonically as it becomes non-relativistic, so the contribution
rem:jerk-neutrinos.title: Massive neutrinos strengthen the bound

rem:residual-boundary-layer.text: The deterministic limit describes $\fconv$; it does not describe $1-\fconv$, and the precursor density is proportional to the latter. From \cref{eq:process-binomial} the relative fluctuation of $1-\fconv$ is $\sqrt{p/[N(1-p)]}$, which \emph{diverges} as $p\to1$. The continuum description of $\rhoI$ therefore fails once the expected number of unconverted units falls below one, at % \begin{keyresult
rem:residual-boundary-layer.title: But the residual density has a boundary layer

rem:sandwich-naive.text: The version of this statement one writes down first is false, so it is worth recording. Bracketing instead by the pair $(\rho_{\rm m}^{\rm early},V_{\rm early})$ does \emph{not} give an upper bound: that model is a lower bound, and it does not share $\Hz$.
rem:sandwich-naive.title: The naive bracketing is wrong

thm:b-independence.text: Under \cref{asm:geodesic}, let $\delta_{\rm m}=\sum_k\bar\rho_k\delta_k/\bar\rho_{\rm m}$ run over all pressureless species $k\in\{I,D,{\rm b}\}$ and let $\vartheta$ be the perturbed expansion. Then for every $\bfrac\in[0,1]$ % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:perturbations-system} \dot\delta_{\rm m}=-\vartheta+\gamma_c\delta_{\rm m}, \qquad \dot\vartheta+2\Hub\vartheta=-\frac{\bar\rho_{\rm m}}{2\Mpl^2}\de
thm:b-independence.title: $\bfrac$-independence of linear growth

thm:bounded-rate-obstruction.text: Let $0\le\Gam\le G<\infty$ on $[\tau_0,T)$ with $T-\tau_0$ finite, and let the compression be non-integrable, $\int^{T}\expa\,\dd s=-\infty$. Then $\rhoI\to\infty$.
thm:bounded-rate-obstruction.title: Bounded rates cannot regularize a caustic

thm:de-sitter.text: Add to \cref{thm:regular-future} either $V_i>0$, or $\bfrac<1$ together with $\rho_{I,i}>0$ and $\int^\infty\Gam\,\dd t=\infty$. Then $\rhoV\to \Vinf>0$, all other densities tend to zero, % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:cosmology-desitter} \Hub(t)\longrightarrow \Hinf=\sqrt{\frac{\Vinf}{3\Mpl^2}}>0, \qquad a(t)e^{-\Hinf(t-t_i)}\longrightarrow C\in(0,\infty) , \end{keyresult} % and the expansion accelera
thm:de-sitter.title: \dS attractor without superacceleration

thm:deterministic-limit.text: Under \cref{asm:rate-regularity}, on every finite time interval the process of \cref{eq:process-intensity} converges in probability to % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:process-deterministic} \dot \fconv=(1-\fconv)\Gam(\fconv,\Mmem), \qquad \tauM\dot \Mmem=\fconv-\Mmem . \end{keyresult}
thm:deterministic-limit.title: Law of large numbers

thm:hysteresis.text: Fix a scale factor $a(t)$ and let $\beta>0$. Let two solutions of \cref{eq:process-deterministic} driven by that $a(t)$ reach the same converted fraction $\fconv_*$ at the same time with different memory states $\Mmem^{(1)}>\Mmem^{(2)}$. Then $\fconv^{(1)}(t)\ge \fconv^{(2)}(t)$ at every later $t$, with strict inequality on a set of positive measure, and the vacuum accumulated through \cref{eq:cos
thm:hysteresis.title: Hysteresis, along a prescribed expansion history

thm:jerk.text: For a spatially flat universe containing pressureless matter, conserved radiation, an exact vacuum that receives energy at rate $\QV$, and any further conserved species whose pressure is non-increasing in time, % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:cosmography-jerk} \jerk=1+2\Omr+\varepsilon , \qquad \varepsilon\eqdef\frac{\QV}{2\Mpl^2\Hub^3} , \end{keyresult} % and therefore, whenever the transfer is towards
thm:jerk.title: Jerk identity and bound

thm:memory-fingerprint.text: At fixed $(\Hz,q_0,j_0)$ the memory parameters are unconstrained by the jerk, and do enter the snap: % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:cosmography-fingerprint} \frac{\partial j_0}{\partial \mathcal B}=0 , \qquad \frac{\partial s_0}{\partial \mathcal B}=+\varepsilon_0\ \ne 0 . \end{keyresult} % The activation term of \cref{eq:cosmography-snap-explicit}, however, enters the same bracket with the \emph{same}
thm:memory-fingerprint.title: Memory fingerprint, and what limits it

thm:no-go.text: Suppose the solution exists with non-negative densities on $[a_i,1]$, that $\Gam\ge\Gamz>0$ throughout, that $\bfrac<1$ and $\rho_{I0}>0$, and that $\Hub$ is non-increasing. Then % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:solvable-nogo} V_0-\rhoV(a_i)\ \ge\ c\,(1-\bfrac)\Mpl^2\,\Gamz \Hub_i , \qquad \Gamz\ \lesssim\ \frac{\Hz^2}{\Hub_i} , \end{keyresult} % with $c=\order{1}$ set by the precursor fraction at $a_i$.
thm:no-go.title: Rate-floor no-go

thm:no-sign-flip.text: Define $\delta_{\rm eff}=\dd\ln(\rhodmeff a^3)/\dd\ln a$. Under \cref{asm:closure} with $\rhodmeff>0$, % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:positivity-no-sign-flip} \delta_{\rm eff}(a)=-\frac{\QV}{\Hub\rhodmeff}=-\xieff(a)\le0 \qquad\text{for every }a , \end{keyresult} % for every admissible rate law, with equality only where $\Gam\rhoI=0$ or $\bfrac=1$. The same holds for the total dust.
thm:no-sign-flip.title: No sign flip

thm:quasi-positivity.text: Assume \cref{asm:closure} with non-negative initial data, and let $\Gam\ge0$ be merely locally integrable along the solution: no lower bound, no upper bound, and no continuity are required. Then the non-negative orthant is forward invariant: every density in \cref{eq:cosmology-system} remains non-negative for as long as the solution exists.
thm:quasi-positivity.title: Quasi-positivity

thm:regular-future.text: Assume \cref{asm:closure}; non-negative initial densities with positive sum; $a_i=1$, $\fconv_i\in[0,1)$, $\Mmem_i\in[0,1]$, $\bfrac\in[0,1]$, $\tauM>0$; and $\Gam$ locally Lipschitz with $0\le\Gam\le G<\infty$ on the physical domain. Then a unique solution exists for all finite future times, all densities remain non-negative, $\fconv,\Mmem\in[0,1]$, $\Hub>0$, and % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:cosmolo
thm:regular-future.title: Regular future

thm:sandwich.text: Let the solution be defined and non-negative on $[a_e,1]$ with radiation exactly conserved, and define the matter deficit % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:positivity-deficit} \Delta\eqdef\frac{\rho_{\rm m}^{\rm early}-\rho_{\rm m0}}{3\Mpl^2\Hz^2} =\frac{1}{3\Mpl^2\Hz^2}\int_{t_e}^{t_0}\QV a^3\,\dd t\ \ge 0 , \qquad \rho_{\rm m}^{\rm early}\eqdef\rhom(t_e)\,a_e^3 , \end{keyresult} % both densities being c
thm:sandwich.title: Sandwich

thm:sign-table.title: Sign table

thm:snap.text: With $\snap=\dot \jerk/\Hub-\jerk(2+3\decel)$ and $\snap_{\LCDM}(\decel,\Omr)=2\Omr'-(1+2\Omr)(2+3\decel)$ its value at $\QV=0$, evaluated at the same $\decel$ and $\Omr$, % \begin{keyresult}{C}{eq:cosmography-snap} \snap-\snap_{\LCDM}(\decel,\Omr) =\varepsilon\left[\frac{\dd\ln\Gam}{\dd \efold}-\frac{\Gam}{\Hub}-2\right] , \end{keyresult} % which for the rate law \cref{eq:process-rate} reads % \b
thm:snap.title: Snap
